title: TCP Three-Way Handshake
body:
Before any [[HTTP]] bytes are sent, the two machines have to agree that a connection exists. TCP does this with a three-step exchange: the client sends **SYN** ("I want to talk, here's my starting sequence number"), the server replies **SYN-ACK** ("acknowledged, and here's mine"), and the client sends **ACK** ("acknowledged"). Only after that third packet is the connection considered open and usable.

In the postal analogy this is the courier physically confirming they've reached the right building and opening a channel before handing anything over. It starts in your machine's OS network stack, passes through your router (doing [[NAT]]), your ISP, and backbone routers, and ends at the destination's infrastructure — usually a [[Load Balancer]], not the final application server. The handshake costs a full round trip, which is why reusing an existing connection for subsequent requests matters so much for performance. The [[TLS Handshake]] happens after this, on top of the now-open TCP connection.
